newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals' mostly up as world markets rise.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals' mostly up as world markets rise.

text.p: Indian zinc prices rose on Tuesday along with lead, tin and nickel while copper and aluminium were unchanged against an uptrend in world markets, dealers said.

Zinc rose by 50 rupees to 6,750 rupees per quintal on limited arrivals. "Reports that state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd. has raised selling prices of zinc by 1,500 rupees per tonne also aided the uptrend," said Sharad Parikh, president of the Bombay Metal Exchange.

Lead rose by 25 rupees to 4,550 rupees per quintal while tin rose by 100 rupees to 34,600 rupees. Nickel rose by 200 rupees to 36,900 rupees per quintal. Copper was steady at 12,650 rupees and aluminium at 7,200 rupees per quintal on nominal trade.
